title: Armor & Helmets (Tables 9.1, 9.2 & 9.3)
text:
Armor is **Mail**, **Plate**, or **Textile** (padding). Textile padding (aketon) is worn under mail.

## Table 9.1 — Suits of Armor (total Armor Protection)

| Typical for | Components | Protection | Shield |
|-------------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| Squire | Gambeson, open helm | 5 | Round (Large) |
| Poor Knights | Mail hauberk, open helm, aketon | 9 | Kite (Large) |
| **Knights** | Mail hauberk, nasal helm, aketon | 10 | Kite (Large) |
| Armored guardsmen & squires | Haubergeon, open helm, aketon | 7 | Kite (Large) |
| Rich knights | Advanced hauberk, advanced nasal helm, aketon | 12 | Kite (Large) |
| Very rich knights (515+) | Coat of plates, advanced hauberk, advanced nasal helm, aketon | 13 | Kite (Large); −5 Move on foot |
| Foot soldiers | Gambeson, kettle helm | 5 | Kite (Large) |
| Saxon footmen | Haubergeon, open helm | 5 | Round (Large) |
| Irish footmen | None | 0 | Simple (Med.) |
| Picts | None | 0 | Buckler (Small) |
| Roman foot soldiers | Haubergeon, advanced nasal helm, aketon | 9 | Scutum (Large) |

A large shield penalizes **−2 to all Weapon Skills when mounted** (except a Charge with spear or lance).

## Table 9.2 — Armor

| Item | Available | Type | Protection | Padding |
|------|-----------|------|-----------|---------|
| Aketon | All | Textile | 2 | None |
| Gambeson | All | Textile | 4 | None |
| Haubergeon | All | Mail | 4 | Aketon |
| Hauberk | All | Mail | 6 | Aketon |
| Advanced Hauberk | Boy King | Mail | 7 | Aketon |
| Coat of Plates | Late Boy King (515+) | Plate | 6 | Aketon |

**Coat of plates** worn over a (advanced) hauberk gives **+1 Armor Protection** and **negates weapon damage bonuses vs Mail** (bonuses vs **Plate** still apply), but imposes **−5 Movement Rate on foot**.

## Table 9.3 — Helmets

| Item | Available | Protection |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| Kettle Helm | All | 1 |
| Open Helm | All | 1 |
| Nasal Helm | All | 2 |
| Advanced Nasal Helm | Boy King | 3 |

Most early helms include a **coif** (mail hood) whose protection is already factored in.

### Closed helms

Closed helms (starting with the Advanced Nasal Helm) impose **−5 to all sight/sound Awareness rolls**. Raising a **visor** nullifies the penalty but **halves the helm's Armor Protection**; a visorless closed helm must be **removed** (1 full Combat Round) to nullify it. Assume visors are down unless stated.

title: Armoring Up, Stacking & Armor Penalties
text:
## Donning armor

Fully arming up (a leisure action, with a squire) takes **5 minutes = 30 Combat Rounds**. Time is **tripled** with no squire, **halved** with two helpers.

In an **emergency**: down to **15 rounds** with a successful **DEX roll and Squire Skill roll**; failing one → **20 rounds**; failing both → full time. The knight may take no other action but communication while donning. **Padding alone** (no squire) takes rounds equal to its Armor Protection value; a **helmet** takes **1 round**.

## Stacking

**All Armor Protection values stack** — total every worn piece for the character's full Armor Protection. You may go into combat **partially armored**.

## Penalties

Wearing armor **never** affects the DEX Balance Roll to stay on foot or mounted.

- **Hot weather:** Combat/Weapon Skills take **−5**, worsening **−1 per consecutive day** of excessive heat to a **max −10**.
- **Sleeping in armor:** sleeping in mail or plate temporarily reduces **all Skills −1 per night**; one good night's sleep out of armor removes it.

title: Shield Damage & Breakage — When a Shield Protects and When It Breaks
text:
In the Pendragon RPG, shields do not have an ongoing pool of structural "Hit Points." Instead, their effectiveness and durability are governed by specific combat rules:

### **1. Standard Shield Protection**

- **Protection Value:** Each shield type has a flat Armor Protection value (generally **6** for Large or Medium shields, and **4** for Small shields).
- **Triggering Shield Protection:** A shield only absorbs damage if you score a **Partial Success** in an opposed combat resolution. If you fail your combat roll or if your opponent wins cleanly, the blow completely bypasses your shield and it provides no protection.
- **Defending Your Mount:** If you are mounted and an opponent intentionally attacks your horse, scoring a partial success allows you to apply your shield's protection value to protect your mount.

### **2. Destroying or Damaging Shields**

Standard high-quality shields (like Kite, Round, or Scutum shields) do not take wear-and-tear damage from normal weapon attacks. However, there are specific situations where a shield can be damaged, degraded, or permanently broken:

- **Axe Attacks (The Anti-Shield Weapon):** Battle Axes, Great Axes, Franciscas, and later Pollaxes are specifically designed to hack through shields. When you are hit by an axe but are able to apply your shield's protection:
    - The shield does not block its full value; instead, it **only blocks 1D6 points of damage** (up to its maximum protection value).
    - If you roll a **1 on that 1D6 block roll**, the shield immediately **breaks and is rendered useless**.
- **Simple Shields (Poor Quality):** If you are carrying a cheap, poorly made **Simple Shield** (typically used by poor infantry) and use its protection value against an opponent's **Critical Success**, the shield **shatters instantly** and is destroyed.
- **Poor Knight Standard of Living:** If a knight falls to a Poor Standard of Living, their neglected gear suffers. All of their armor (including their shield) has its protection value **permanently reduced by 1 point**.
- **Ritual Disgrace:** If a knight's Honor falls to zero, they are stripped of their rank. In a public ceremony of disgrace, their shield is **ceremonially smashed**, their sword broken, and their spurs cut off.

---

🛡️ I can detail the specific differences between the Kite, Round, Heater, and Targe shields—including their unique missile attack penalties and mounted combat modifiers.

title: Shields (Types & Table 9.4)
text:
Shields need **no separate Skill** and are used with one-handed weapons. A shield gives its Armor Value when the wielder scores a **partial success** (a failure lets the hit **bypass** it). A **mounted** character may apply Shield Protection to their **horse** on a partial success. An aware shield-user imposes a **Missile Attack Penalty** on archers.

## Shield sizes

| Size | Armor Protection | Missile penalty | Notes |
|------|-----------------|-----------------|-------|
| **Small** | 4 (melee only, not vs Mounted Charge) | none | useless vs missiles |
| **Medium** | 6 | −5 | compromise |
| **Large** | 6 | −10 | **−2 Weapon Skill mounted** (except as noted) |

## Table 9.4 — Individual shields

- **Buckler (Small)** — center-grip round/oval; **+1D6 damage** to a Barehand punch while held; may be **dropped free** at a round's start.
- **Targe (Small)** — strapped to the forearm (hand free for javelins / a second weapon / a two-handed grip — but then gives **no protection**); **cannot be dropped**; doesn't hamper Grappling/Brawling; no punch bonus.
- **Simple (Medium)** — poor infantry shield; **shatters** if it blocks a **critical success** (useless afterward).
- **Round (Large)** — infantry/Saxon shield, central grip behind a boss.
- **Kite (Large)** — teardrop; the standard knightly shield of the Boy King Period. **Ignores the −2 mounted penalty** when used with a couched spear/lance in a Mounted Charge; designed to also protect against arrows.
- **Scutum (Large)** — oval Roman shield with brackets holding weighted javelins (*plumbatae*).

title: Character Progression & "Winning the Game"
text:
Characters change over time: Skills improve, Traits/Passions rise and fall, Characteristics diminish with age. Advancement is variable; most never climb the whole ladder, and gaining a **noble title** is exceedingly rare. Parenthesized steps are optional.

- **Knights:** Squire → (Esquire) → Mercenary Knight *or* Household Knight → (Officer) → Vassal Knight → (Courtier) → Banneret Knight → (Noble Title)
- **Ladies:** Handmaiden → Lady → (Noble Title) → Gentlewoman

## "Winning the game"

A player may set a **lifelong ambition** and, on reaching it, **retire** the character to personal fulfillment — they've "won." Such a character may still be played when action occurs near their retirement, when their particular Skill is needed, or when everyone is mustered for a battle.

title: Glory — Distribution (Table 6.1), Gaining, Benchmarks & Challenges
text:
Glory is fame accumulated for deeds. **Only nobles gain it; it can increase but never decrease** — successful *bad* behavior adds Glory as surely as good (bad behavior costs Honor, not Glory). Glory requires **public acclamation** (secret deeds earn none) and decides **precedence** when other factors are equal, but never overrides rank (a count with 3,000 outranks a baron with 5,000). **Every 1,000 Glory → one Prestige Reward** (Winter Phase, Step 10).

## Table 6.1 — Glory Distribution

| Glory | Prominence | ~% of knights |
|-------|-----------|---------------|
| < 3,000 | Unproven | 10 |
| 3,000–3,999 | Veteran | 45 |
| 4,000–5,999 | Respected | 30 |
| 6,000–7,999 | Notable | 10 |
| 8,000–11,999 | Renowned | 3 |
| 12,000–15,999 | Illustrious | 2 |
| 16,000–31,999 | Extraordinary | negligible |
| 32,000+ | Legendary | minuscule |

## Gaining Glory — benchmarks

Any non-routine act with notable, **public** consequences may win Glory. **Never award more than 1,000 for a single event**, though separate awards can combine past 1,000.

- **25** (slightly risky): defeat bandits; defeat a foe with Skill 15.
- **50** (dangerous): defeat a foe with Skill 20.
- **100** (heroic): kill a panther; save your liege's life.
- **250** (extraordinary): kill a dangerous monster (large giant, gryphon); win the Pentecost Tournament; become a vassal knight.
- **300–500** (mighty): kill a fearsome monster (gargantuan giant, wyrm); become a banneret.
- **1,000** (once-in-a-lifetime): become a knight; become a great lord; join the Round Table; attend the Mass of the Holy Grail.
- **None:** routine with no risk/consequence.

## "Do You Know Who I Am?" — challenges

A knight refusing a fight normally loses 1 Honor for cowardice, **but** a knight of greater rank or **≥5,000 Glory more** may decline an inferior's challenge without risk (backing down from a **social better** earns a **Prudent** check; declining a challenge "to the death" also earns a **Cowardly** check).

To fight a social better, the inferior must master fear: roll **Valorous** at **−1 per 1,000 Glory difference (max −5)**; they may first roll **Prudent** at **+1 per 1,000 (max +5)** to back down honorably. A disguised knight (hidden/changed arms) imposes **−10 to Recognize**. A Round Table Knight may ride through an enemy formation, intimidating all so none dares approach.

title: Honor — Nature, Ranges, Gaining & Oaths
text:
Honor is a noble's integrity/worth and the public trust and recognition granted to them. It is inborn to nobles (not needed by churchmen or commoners), upholds social norms (respect superiors, uphold a lord's name, loyalty, hospitality, class rules), and includes a personal code that **demands a response if questioned**. It **cannot be seized/bought/traded — only granted** by others recognizing it. **Glory without Honor is the mark of an unworthy wretch.**

- **Ranges (1–20):** Unsung 1–4, Normal 5–15, Famous 16–20, Exalted 20+x.
- **Below 5 Honor** → lose title, cast out of noble society. **Honor 0** → disgraced forever, removed from play (can never be raised again).
- May be used **exactly like a Passion** to gain a bonus to one Skill when defending Honor (see [[core.traits-passions.passion-roll-inspiration-and-crisis]]).

## Public vs. private Honor

Honor measures what the **public** knows. Secret dishonorable acts are noted as a parenthetical negative, e.g. `Honor 14 (−3)`. **All Honor rolls use the true value** (modified by hidden dishonor); if the acts are exposed, the parenthetical is permanently subtracted. The GM may rule that a private honor-gaining/losing deed causes **no change until exposed**.

## Gaining Honor

Via experience checks — an honorable deed **beyond normal duty**, usually per a Trait/Passion. Examples (with the enabling Trait):

- Clemency to a foe who didn't ask (Forgiving); alms ≥£10 / like donation / ≥1/10 of a non-relative's ransom (Generous); keeping a secret under torture (Honest); a lawful decision against self-interest (Just); mercy to a knight who didn't ask (Merciful); sharing fresh Glory with fellows (Modest); upholding religion under adversity (Spiritual); valorous battle feats — re-entering under half HP, fighting on when others flee, taking up a fallen standard, surviving 3:1 odds, winning the battle (Valorous); keeping the peace under Hospitality; defending a liege / obeying against self-preservation (Homage); obeying an unwise order (Fealty/Loyalty); holding order vs a mob (Station).

## Defending Honor

When someone **publicly** questions/insults your Honor or a deeply-held virtue, you **must act or lose Honor** (a Chivalrous knight whose valor is doubted; a Religious knight whose faith is mocked). You must also defend the Honor of family, liege, and king.

## Oaths

An oath is a promise under divine witness — the most sacred bond; breakers are shunned. Make an appropriate **Passion roll** when taking an important oath; Honor at stake: **Critical 3, Success 2, Failure 1, Fumble 0.** A PK may have only **one active oath** at a time.

- **Positive oath** (vow to accomplish): gain the staked Honor on success; **lose** it on failure.
- **Negative oath** (vow never to do): **immediately gain** the staked Honor, but **lose double** if ever broken.

title: Ideals — Chivalrous, Religious & Romantic Knight
text:
Ideals grant **bonuses** for maintaining minimum values in prescribed Skills, Passions, and Traits. Most are realized through action (not bestowal); benefits accrue as soon as qualified and **lapse if a requirement drops below minimum**. Some Ideals are mutually exclusive; others may be held together.

## Chivalrous Knight

**Benefits:** may invoke the **Chivalry** Passion when offended vs the Code; **Armor of Virtue** = 4 points of Armor Protection that blocks *all* damage (even damage that bypasses armor — falls, fire); **150 Passive Glory/year**; **Protection from Magic & Miracles** — a Chivalry roll (success/critical) grants immunity to any supernatural effect that would force a breach of the Code.

**Requirements:**
- Chivalrous **Traits** total **96** among: Energetic, Generous, Just, Merciful, Modest, Valorous (no per-Trait minimum — an average high quality).
- **Chivalry 15, Station 10, Hospitality 10.** Deliberately violating the Code may cost the Ideal.

## Religious Knight

**Benefits (by faith):** Christian **+4 Total HP**; Pagan **+2 Damage, +2 Healing Rate**; Wodinic **+1D6 Damage**; Heathen **+2 Movement, +1 Healing Rate**. Plus: may invoke **Devotion (Deity)** in defense of the faith; **100 Passive Glory/year**; **Protection from Magic & Miracles** — a Devotion roll (success/critical) grants immunity to magic (if Christian) or miracles (if Pagan/Wodinic/Heathen).

**Requirements:** value **16 in all six** virtuous Traits of the faith —
- Christian: Chaste, Forgiving, Merciful, Modest, Spiritual, Temperate
- Pagan: Energetic, Generous, Honest, Lustful, Proud, Spiritual
- Wodinic: Generous, Indulgent, Proud, Reckless, Valorous, Worldly
- Heathen: Arbitrary, Honest, Proud, Spiritual, Suspicious, Vengeful

— plus **Devotion (Deity) 16** and **Religion 10**.

## Romantic Knight

The champion of Love (above duty/Honor); a practitioner of *fine amor* (a **Lover** with an Adoration for their **Beloved**).

**Benefits:** always finds favor at Queen Guenever's court (may join the Queen's Knights on request); **+2 base Geniality** always; **double Glory at tournaments** when wearing the Beloved's favor; **Protection from Magic & Miracles** — an Adoration roll (success/critical) grants immunity to any effect that would make them harm/betray the Beloved.

**Requirements:** Romantic **Traits** total **90** among Chaste, Generous, Honest, Modest, Spiritual (as a Directed Trait toward the Beloved), Temperate; plus **Adoration (Beloved) 10**.

title: Losing Honor — Violations, Accusation, Grievous Dishonor & Flight
text:
It is far easier to lose Honor than gain it. When a violation occurs, the GM either docks Honor immediately or has the PK roll the **opposing** Trait/Passion — on a **success** they lose the Honor and check the opposing Trait.

## Honor loss by acting against Traits/Passions

- **−1:** seduce a married noble / cuckold (Chaste); idle in a crisis (Energetic); lie/cheat/steal (Honest); skip a feast in your honor or refuse a toast (Indulgent); virility questioned (Lustful); over-boast (Modest); first scolding by Sir Kay (Proud); hold back (Reckless); dress as a commoner / insult or provoke a noble (Station); disobey liege on a small matter (Homage/Fealty); insult a guest/host (Hospitality).
- **−2:** be cuckolded (Chaste); defraud/slander (Just); attack an unarmed knight or kill one who begged mercy / was ransomable (Merciful); chronic glutton/drunk or vomit at a feast (Temperate); use missiles vs a knight or set lethal traps (Valorous); refuse/argue an order (Fealty/Homage); defer to a wealthy commoner / embarrass a noble (Station); physically harm a guest (Hospitality).
- **−3:** perjury (Just); deliberately harm a lady (Merciful); flee a fair fight / surrender to an equal (Valorous); refuse aid to family (Love Family); disobey liege on a significant matter (Fealty/Homage); harm your host (Hospitality); do commoner's work (Station).
- **−4:** kidnap a lady (Merciful); survive your liege's death as his bodyguard (Valorous); defer to a poor commoner (Station).
- **−5:** break an oath (Honest); kill a lady or holy person of your faith (Spiritual); kill by poison (Valorous); cause a battle loss in a liege's service (Fealty/Homage); kill a guest/host (Hospitality).
- **−10:** unjustly kill a family member (Love Family); **betray your liege** — reveal secrets, harm, kill, oppose in battle (Fealty/Homage).

Also: **inaction** (ignoring others' dishonor, or failing to avenge an insult/slain family) = −1; **losing** a formal honor-challenge = −1; **killing a surrendered knight** = −5 (**−10 if Chivalrous**).

## Accusation (formal stages)

An accusation by a **reliable source** (equal/greater status, Honorable, credible witness), made before peers, proceeds in stages — each an accuser's roll opposed by the accused's Honor, up to a year apart. The accuser stakes **1–10 Honor**.

1. **Gossip** (Intrigue) → 2. **Public Accusation** (Orate) → 3. **Testimony**, sworn on relics/sword (Just) → 4. **Guilt** proven/disproven (special — often trial of arms, argument before the liege, or word-vs-word Honor roll). Proven → accused loses the stake; disproven → **accuser** loses it.

**Overlooking petty issues:** a knight may ignore an inferior's accusation (a known liar, or someone with < half their Glory) with a successful unopposed **Honor** roll.

## Grievous Dishonor (instant −10, often plus punishment)

Breaking & entering; Fratricide/Sororicide; Murder (perfidious killing outside honorable combat); Parricide (→ outlawry; intentional → loss of all Honor & knighthood); Rape (capital); Rebellion/Treason (capital); **Working Magic** (→ loss of knightly status).

## False claims (regaining Honor via apology)

- **Gossip** → public apology (both check Forgiving & Courtesy on acceptance).
- **Public accusation** → public retraction on the knees (Courtesy/Modest checks); if not forgiven, the accuser loses Honor equal to the victim's loss (victim checks Vengeful; if forgiven, Forgiving).
- **False testimony** → public humiliation, blows, reparations, a cleric's scourging; if mercy denied, the miscreant takes the same Honor loss they caused.

## Honorable Flight

A knight **must** risk death to save the king, their liege, or family. Acting for themselves, they may flee — no shame from a dragon, a real giant, or 5:1 odds (fleeing merely-outnumbering bandits at 5:1 is cowardly, −1 Honor). Prudent withdrawal is fine at **half Total HP**, **2:1 odds or worse** by equal forces, as a ruse, or to diminish danger.

title: Knight of the Round Table
text:
The Round Table is unveiled at Arthur's wedding in **514**; a **siege** (seat) is the most prestigious honor in the land, offered **only by King Arthur himself**. Four kinds hold sieges: **Chivalrous** paragons; ordinary knights who accomplish great deeds (most PKs); Arthur's relations and allied kings' children; and redemption-project "guests of the crown" (wards/hostages).

## Benefits

- **+5 Honor** on obtaining the siege.
- **1,000 Glory** on taking the oath.
- Annual gift of **£10**.
- Membership as a **Household Knight of King Arthur** (keeping prior honors): mutual protection (no member may harm another), a private house in Camelot with seven servants, upkeep as a **Rich knight**, the best steeds and armor.
- A siege with the knight's name written **magically in gold**.

## Requirements

There must be a **vacancy** (a member dies or is banished — rare after the Peace of Arthur until the Grail Quest; GM's call). The knight must be **noticed and invited** by Arthur — most likely for **Renowned (8,000+ Glory)**, having achieved the **Chivalry** Ideal, or an extraordinary deed. Suggested minimum Passions: **Honor 15, Homage (King Arthur) 16, Devotion (Deity) 10, Station 10, Hospitality 10, Chivalry 15.**

## Duties & expulsion

A member is expected to be a paragon of Arthur's ideals, do the king's bidding, and attend Camelot every **Pentecost**; otherwise their life continues as before (same lands, same associates, adventuring with the other PKs).

**Expulsion** follows a witnessed dishonorable crime brought to Arthur and a trial by peers: the golden name vanishes, gifts are reclaimed, family cast out, retainer canceled, exile from Camelot, and **−10 Honor** (plus the trial's loss). If Honor hits 0, they are stripped of knighthood in a public degradation (shield smashed, sword broken, spurs cut off) and named enemy of the Round Table — any good knight may take their life. They are recommended to an abbey to expiate their sins under the church's protection.
