title: Battle Foe Encounters — Pictish Clansmen & Saxon Warriors (the Shield Wall)
text:
## Pictish Clansmen — Morale Loss 1D6+1 · Minimum 8 · KV 1/8

Painted men from beyond the Wall, common in the army of Lothian and other Northern kingdoms. No armor but their tattoos and a targe on the wrist; no weapon but a spear, always two-handed. ==They care nothing for ransoms and offer none — a knight's head on a pike is reward enough.==

- **Two Pictish Clansmen per Player-knight.**
- Spears are **two-handed** (the damage already reflects the bonus). They may use **Set Spear** against a Mounted Charge ==**without needing a roll**== — they are trained in the tactic as a matter of self-preservation.
- **Their tattoos are not magical and give no Armor Protection**, whatever they believe.
- Once **one-third** are seriously wounded or slain, the rest **Evade** on the next round.

| SIZ | DEX | STR | CON | | HP | Knockdown | Major Wound | Unconscious |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | 14 | 10 | 12 | | 24 | 12 | 12 | 6 |

**Attack:** Spear (2H) 14, **6D6** · **Movement** 17 · **AP** 4 · **Glory** 25 · **Armor:** targe shield

## Saxon Warriors — Morale Loss 1D6+2 · Minimum 8 · KV 1/4

A band of seasoned, armored **heorthgeneat** — the personal household guard of a Saxon lord.

- **Two Saxons per Player-knight.** One roll sets the collective armament of the **Defending** Saxons.
- ==**The shield wall.**== Each pair is one **Defender** (spear, axe, or sword **plus shield**) and one partner with a **two-handed axe and no shield**. They form a shield wall to **Defend against a Mounted Charge in the first Combat Round** — ==on that first round **only the Defending Saxons roll**.== After the first round, **both Saxons attack normally**.
- ==**They do not accept surrender or ransom.** They fight until **three-quarters** of their number are down and out of the fight.==

| SIZ | DEX | STR | CON | | HP | Knockdown | Major Wound | Unconscious |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 15 | 10 | 15 | 15 | | 30 | 15 | 15 | 8 |

**Attacks (all Skill 14):** Battle Axe (Hafted) **5D6**\* · Spear **5D6**\*\* · Sword **5D6** · Great Axe (2H Hafted) **7D6**\* \* −1D6 Shield Protection · \*\* negates the height penalty for fighting mounted opponents

**Movement** 18 · **AP** 5+6 (or 5 with the Great Axe) · **Glory** 25 · **Armor:** haubergeon, open helm + round shield; **no shield if armed with a Great Axe**

> **Note:** the Saxon **spear** is listed as negating the mounted height penalty even though the Defender also carries a shield. The general rule in the Core Rulebook (ch. 7) grants that negation only to a **two-handed** spear or halberd, which cannot be used with a shield. Treat this as a foe-specific exception as printed.

title: Plunder (Tables 6.9 & 6.10) & the Chance of Countercharge
text:
## Plunder

Player-knights may take **personal plunder** from captured foes and from raids on the enemy baggage train, as detailed in the relevant Encounters; those ransoms already account for the lord's share, the value of kit (armor, weapons, tack), and so on.

**Every participant** also receives a share of the overall loot **if the outcome is a Victory or Decisive Victory**. Unless the scenario says otherwise, the base value is set by the opposing army.

### Table 6.9 — Basic Plunder

| Opponents | Basic plunder | Why |
|---|---:|---|
| Feudal army | £2 | The enemy is the equivalent of the Player-knights |
| Inferior feudal army | £1½ | Distant lands are less well-equipped and mounted |
| Saxons | £1 | Good armor, but the lack of horses affects value |
| Cymric hill tribes | £½ | Inferior arms and horses |
| Pict hill tribes, Irish warriors | £¼ | Poor people, poor armor, virtually no horses |

**On a Decisive Victory, add +£2D3** to the value of the plunder.

### Table 6.10 — Plunder Modifiers

| Circumstance | Modifier |
|---|---|
| Greatly outnumbered the enemy (2:1 or more) | **×½** |
| Own force greatly outnumbered (1:2 or worse) | **×2** |
| Conroi Commander | **+⅓** |
| Division Leader | **×3 × Battle Size Multiplier** |
| Army Leader | **×10 × Battle Size Multiplier** |

**Battle Size Multiplier:** Small ×1 · Medium ×2 · Large ×3 · Huge ×4.

## Chance of Countercharge

Opponents armed with lances — **mounted knights, mounted sergeants, Northern prickers** — **always countercharge** the Player-knights if encountered on the **first Battle Turn**.

On **subsequent turns**, roll **1D6**:

- **1–2:** Yes — they still have lances and the room to countercharge.
- **3–6:** No — their lances are shattered, or they saw the danger too late.

## Choosing Encounters

The Foe Encounters and Opportunities in this chapter are a menu, not a fixed list. Choose from them as described under "Encounters" (GM Book pp. 122–123), or use them as models for your own. **Foes** may recur; **Opportunities** come once and are reachable only on a **critical Battle roll**.

title: Running a Battle — Organization, Intensity, Morale & Commander Rolls
text:
## Army organization

- **Conroi** — 10–15 knights + squires led by a banneret; the **only level that directly affects PKs**. The leader makes tactical decisions.
- **Bataille** (battalion) — several conrois under a baron (typically 3).
- **Army** — split into **three divisions**: vanguard (right), main/middle guard (center, with the commander & supply train), rearguard (left). Divisional and army commanders stay **behind** their troops with reserves.

## Before the battle

GM determines the forces, designates one **Army Commander** per side and their **Battle Skill** (roll **2D6+10** if unknown), sets **Battle Size & Intensity**, and builds two Encounter decks (**Foes** and **Opportunities**). Players set their conroi's makeup, leadership, and **Morale**.

### Table 6.1 — Battle Size

| Size | Knights/side | Combatants | Max turns | Random Intensity |
|------|-------------|-----------|-----------|------------------|
| Fight | 10 | 30 | 1 | 1D6+2 |
| Skirmish | 30 | 100 | 3 | 2D6 |
| Clash | 50 | 300 | 5 | 2D6+1 |
| Small Battle | 150 | 1,000 | 6 | 2D6+2 |
| Medium Battle | 500 | 3,000 | 7 | 2D6+3 |
| Large Battle | 1,500 | 10,000 | 8 | 3D6 |
| Huge Battle | 5,000 | 30,000 | 8 | 3D6+1 |

## Encounters

Battles are built from **Encounters** (vignettes). **Foes** may recur; **Opportunities** come once and are only chosen on a **critical Battle roll** (seize a standard, kill a commander). Higher Intensity = the PKs must react more to the GM's choices.

## Conroi Morale

Choose one shared Passion (or same-court Passions, usually Fidelitas) as the conroi's **Morale** = the **average** of the members' values (**+5 if all pick the same Passion**). Morale drops as they fight, rises by defeating foes and Retiring to the Rear, and **can never exceed its starting value**. Each Encounter has a **Minimum Morale** to engage — below it, the conroi must Retire to the Rear.

## Army Commander Rolls (Clash+)

Each commander rolls **Battle Skill** with **Table 6.2** modifiers:

| Circumstance | Modifier |
|--------------|----------|
| Outnumber 1½:1 / 2:1 / 3:1 / 5:1 | +2/−2 · +5/−5 · +7/−7 · +10/−10 |
| Fighting in own Homeland | +5 |
| Last Stand | +5 (no stack with Homeland) |
| Scouts (≥1/5 KV as hobilars/prickers) | +5 (no stack with Homeland) |
| Fatigued (forced march / hot weather) | −5/+5 |
| Disease / hunger | −5/+5 |
| Multiple fractious commanders | −5 |

**Results:** friendly commander **success/critical → first turn is a mounted charge**; **fumble → whole army −5 Battle** turn 1. Enemy **success/critical → GM forces one Encounter** (once/battle); **fumble → conroi commander may negate one Encounter's Morale effect**.

title: Glory for Combat, Beasts, Adventures & Valor (Table A.1)
text:
How much Glory to award is always the GM's call; these are the book's suggestions. Adapt them to the Glory progression you want, but stick to them for a first campaign.

## Combat Glory — Table A.1

Awarded for **defeating** an opponent (surrendered, killed, disabled, or driven from the fight), based on the opponent's **highest modified Combat Skill used in the fight**.

| Opponent's modified weapon value | Glory |
|---|---:|
| 1–5 | 1 |
| 6–10 | 10 |
| 11–15 | 25 |
| 16–20 | 50 |
| 20 (+1)–20 (+5) | 100 |
| 20 (+6)–20 (+10) | 200 |
| 20 (+11)–20 (+20) | 400 |

Use the **highest** modified value that applied at any point: a knight with Sword 15 who becomes Impassioned counts as Sword 20, moving the award from 25 to 100. A **penalty** suffered for only part of the fight does **not** reduce the award.

**Combat "for love"** — ⅒ the normal Combat Glory. A fight is "for love" if **both sides use rebated weapons**, it is **to first knockdown or first blood**, it is **for honor**, or the prize is **worth £3 or less**.

**Against beasties and fairies** — the award is **divided among all knights** who defeated the creature:

| Creature | Glory | | Creature | Glory |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Dragon | 1,000 | | Cockatrice | 100 |
| Giant (large) | 250 | | Hag | 75 |
| Lion | 250 | | Ogre | 75 |
| Unicorn | 250 | | Bear | 50 |
| Barguest | 100 | | Wolf | 10 |
| | | | Vicious rat | 0 |

**Battles** award Glory by size, victory/defeat, and command, *plus* Combat Glory for the individual foes fought — see [[gm.battle.after-the-battle]].

## Skill use

Skills grant Glory only when used in **significant, public** venues — **a success without witnesses does not count**. Some Skills award only in specific circumstances (First Aid that brings a character back to life or saves a ranking noble).

**Glory = the character's APP.** **Doubled** on a critical, or when performing before a **king or queen**.

## Successful adventure

Awarded for completing a task, and stacking with Glory for enemies defeated. If several characters take part, **each** receives the full award.

- **Simple adventure, easily achieved:** 100
- **Regular adventure:** 200–300
- **Difficult adventure:** 300–500

## Personal valor

- **Winning combat against knights at 4:1 odds or greater:** double the normal award
- **Volunteering for a suicide mission:** +250
- **Dying performing a heroic action:** +1,000

## Afflictions

Involuntary but temporary emotional states that significantly impair the character:

- **Madness:** 100 · **Melancholy:** 25 · **Miserable:** 10

title: Passive Glory (Standard of Living, Traits & Passions) and Glory for Ladies
text:
**Passive Glory** accrues annually in the Winter Phase for what a character *is* and *maintains*, rather than for what they did.

## Standard of Living — Table A.2

A landed knight's Standard of Living is a fraction of total income (**10% of landholdings, plus £5 if married or £4 if unmarried**). It covers personal maintenance only; a household is funded separately.

Living **above** the minimum required for Ordinary is **Conspicuous Consumption**: **10 Glory per additional £1** spent over the annual minimum of **£6** (for a knight with a squire and family). Living **below** one's normal standard carries penalties — see "Standard of Living", Core Rulebook pp. 227–228.

| Title | Typical landholding income | Upkeep | Standard of Living | Passive Glory |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| Vassal Knight | £10 (£7–£30) | £6 | Ordinary | 0 |
| Estate Holder | £50 (£30–£100) | £10 | Rich | 40 |
| Banneret Knight | £100 (£60–£120) | £15 | Superlative | 90 |
| Minor Baron\* | £150 (£100–£200) | £20 | Superlative | 100 |
| Baron | £300 (£200–£400) | £35 | Superlative | 120 |
| Rich Baron\* | £600 (£400–£800) | £65 | Superlative | 150 |
| Count, Duke (Great Baron\*) | £1,000 (£800–£1,600) | £105 | Superlative | 200 |
| King of a major kingdom† | £3,000 (£1,000–£5,000) | £305 | Superlative | 400 |

\* Not official titles — used to quantify a baron's wealth and power. † Cornwall, Malahaut, Lothian. Britain's many minor and petty kings are barely equal to barons in Logres.

## Traits and Passions

- **Famous** (16–20) Traits and Passions: **15 Glory each** per year.
- **Exalted** (20+x): **25 Glory each** per year.
- **Cap: 100 points** of Passive Glory per year from Traits, and **100** from Passions, counted separately.
- ==**Directed Traits and Obsessions generate no Passive Glory.**==

## Ideals

Some Ideals grant Passive Glory when fulfilled, as stated in their own descriptions — see [[core.aspirations.ideals]].

## Glory for Ladies

Ladies receive **the same awards as knights**, plus these:

- **Child born:** 100
- **Eldest child is knighted:** 500 · **any other child knighted:** 100
- **Any son or daughter takes a Title:** ⅒ the Glory of that title's award
- **First son to join the clergy:** 100
- **Eldest son is married:** 250

title: Glory for Honors, Titles, Offices, Expenditure & Special Circumstances
text:
## Honors and titles

- **Knighthood:** 1,000 — **plus** a separate award equal to **1% of the Glory of the lord who knights them**. Being knighted by Arthur is worth far more than by a minor lord.
- **Knight of the Round Table:** 1,000
- **Joining another chivalric organization:** 200

**Titles** award **once per title**, and multiple titles accumulate. Least to greatest:

| Title | Glory | | Title | Glory |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Household Knight | 50 | | Count | 1,000 |
| Vassal Knight | 250 | | Duke | 1,000 |
| Banneret | 500 | | Petty King | 1,000 |
| Baron | 1,000 | | Minor King | 1,000 |
| | | | King of Malahaut / Logres / High King | 1,000 |

**Offices** award **once per liege lord**, scaled to that lord's status, and **once per level of rank** — a knight who becomes steward to a baron gains 100 and gains nothing further for later being made that baron's marshall.

- **Officer to a baron:** 100 · **to a count or duke:** 200 · **to the Pendragon:** 400
- **Privy Councilor:** +100

## Sharing wealth

- **Money to your liege lord** to offset his responsibilities: **10 Glory per £1**, max
  100. Checks **Homage, Generous, Worldly**.
- **Public works** (city walls, baths, market): **5 Glory per £1**, max 100. Checks **Generous** and **Station**.
- **Ransoming a non-family member:** **10 Glory per £1**, max 100. Checks **Generous** and **Just** — and ==the ransomed person gains a **Loyalty** Passion toward the donor equal to the libra value of the ransom paid.==

## Extravagant spending

Totalled across the year in the **Winter Phase**, then converted: **10 Glory per £1 up to 100 Glory**, and **1 Glory per £1** thereafter.

The display must be massive, outrageous, and bring **no return or benefit** beyond Glory, a **Generous** check, and one other appropriate Trait. Naming the specific extravagance is required — "I spend the money" is not enough.

| Spend | Glory | Example (and the Trait checked) |
|---|---:|---|
| £10 | 100 | A grand feast for 300 nobles or 1,000 commoners (**Generous**); a feast for 30 nobles of rare imported meats (**Worldly**); *Gala Bohort!* — a "Kill the Beast" contest with caged wild animals fought with daggers (**Cruel**) |
| £25 | 115 | *Trojan Games!* — ancient sports, knightly (horse race, eating contest, "Odysseus' Bow") and common (javelin, wrestling, cart races) (**Proud**) |
| £50 | 140 | A feast for 30 nobles consisting **only of spices** (**Indulgent**); *Money Wagon!* — devils clearing the way, trumpeters, angels flinging ha'pence (**Arbitrary**) |
| £100 | 190 | *Field of Riches!* — bears harnessed to a plough while women in "Pagan costume" sow droplets of silver (**Reckless**) |

## Building and endowing houses of worship

**Building:** Glory = **10× the structure's cost**, max 500. Checks **Spiritual** and the appropriate **Religion** Skill.

- Small church £25 (250) · Small abbey £52 (500) · Nunnery £23 (230) · Pagan temple £28 (280) · Pagan shrine £25 (250)

**Endowment** (permanently donating land or wealth to a foundation): Glory = **100× the value of the land**, max 500. Checks **Generous**, **Spiritual**, and the **Religion** Skill. The donor also earns a **Favor** from the head of the institution worth the construction and land combined.

- Small church £3 (300) · Small abbey £7 (500) · Nunnery £3 (300) · Pagan temple £6 (500) · Pagan shrine £3 (300)

## Special circumstances

- **Knighting a squire of greater social rank:** 100 · **heir to a king:** 250
- **Refusing rank** — declining an offer of land or title from a grateful monarch: **250 Glory** immediately. The rebuffed party's reaction is the GM's to decide.
- **Marriage:** Glory equal to **¼ of the spouse's Glory**, up to 1,000.

## Tournaments

- **Sponsoring:** Glory = the cost × the **Extravagant Spending** bonus.
- **Attending, participating, winning:** everyone gains Glory; amounts vary by the size of the tournament (see *Tournaments*, GM Book p. 51).
- **The Melee** is almost always fought *for love* → **⅒ normal Combat Glory**. For greater stakes (the loser's horse, large Favors, ransom) but still rebated weapons → **½ normal**. Mordred's "Blood Tournaments", with unrebated weapons, pay **full Combat Glory**.
- **Jousting:** Glory is set by the prize's value and figured **per round, not per pass**. Prize ≤ £3 → as a regular joust. Prize > £3 → **half the opponent's Charge Skill** per round.

## Witnessing and hosting special events

The **host** of the event receives **five times** the witness's award.

- **£2 baptism of an heir:** 10 (20 for godparents)
- **£1 baptism of another child:** 5 (10 for godparents)
